stem: Madhubani (Mithila) painting originates from the state of __________.
solution: Madhubani (Mithila) painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar.

stem: Madhubani painting was traditionally done by women on the __________.
solution: Madhubani painting was traditionally done by women on the walls and floors of homes.

stem: Warli painting is a tribal art form from the state of __________.
solution: Warli painting is a tribal art of Maharashtra.

stem: Warli paintings are characterised by __________ figures on a mud-red background.
solution: Warli art uses simple white geometric figures (triangles, circles, lines) on an earthy background.

stem: Pattachitra painting is a traditional cloth-based scroll painting of __________.
solution: Pattachitra is a traditional scroll (cloth) painting of Odisha and West Bengal.

stem: Pattachitra paintings mostly depict themes related to __________.
solution: Pattachitra mostly depicts Lord Jagannath and Vaishnava themes.

stem: Kalighat painting developed in the 19th century near a temple in __________.
solution: Kalighat painting developed near the Kalighat temple in Calcutta.

stem: Phad painting, a scroll art depicting folk deities, belongs to __________.
solution: Phad is a scroll painting tradition of Rajasthan depicting folk deities like Pabuji.

stem: Gond painting is a tribal art form associated with __________.
solution: Gond painting is a tribal art of the Gond community, mainly in Madhya Pradesh.

stem: Kalamkari is a form of __________ done with natural dyes.
solution: Kalamkari is a hand-painted or block-printed cotton textile art using natural dyes.

stem: Kalamkari is traditionally practised in __________.
solution: Kalamkari (Srikalahasti and Machilipatnam styles) is from Andhra Pradesh/Telangana.

stem: Pichwai paintings, made on cloth to hang behind the idol of Shrinathji, come from __________.
solution: Pichwai paintings are made at Nathdwara in Rajasthan, depicting Shrinathji (Krishna).

stem: Thangka paintings are associated with __________ Buddhism.
solution: Thangka is a Tibetan Buddhist scroll painting tradition of the Himalayan region.

stem: The colours used in most folk and tribal paintings are __________.
solution: Folk and tribal paintings traditionally use natural mineral and vegetable dyes.

stem: The 'living' art traditions are so called because they __________.
options: are still practised by communities today
solution: They are 'living' traditions because they are still practised by communities today.

stem: Madhubani painting is characterised by __________.
options: intricate patterns, double lines and filling every space
solution: Madhubani has intricate patterns, bold double-line outlines and densely filled compositions.

stem: Warli painting is traditionally associated with __________ occasions.
solution: Warli painting is linked with weddings, harvests and community rituals.

stem: The central motif in many Warli paintings is the __________.
solution: The spiral 'tarpa dance' of figures is a central Warli motif.

stem: Kalighat paintings are known for their __________.
options: bold, sweeping brushwork and social satire
solution: Kalighat paintings are known for bold brushwork, simple forms and social satire.

stem: Folk and tribal art forms are important sources of __________ for the communities that make them.
solution: These art forms provide cultural identity and livelihood for their communities.

stem: The Cheriyal scroll paintings come from the state of __________.
solution: Cheriyal scroll paintings are a folk tradition of Telangana.

stem: The Manjusha painting tradition, on a scroll, belongs to __________.
solution: Manjusha painting is a scroll folk art from Bhagalpur, Bihar.

stem: Many folk and tribal art forms have received __________ tags to protect their identity.
solution: Several folk arts have received Geographical Indication (GI) tags.

stem: Folk paintings differ from courtly miniatures in that they are __________.
options: community-based and rooted in daily life and ritual
solution: Folk paintings are community-based, rooted in daily life and ritual, unlike courtly miniatures.

stem: The Pattachitra artists are called __________.
solution: Pattachitra painters are traditionally called chitrakars.

stem: Warli art is done using a paste of __________ as the white pigment.
solution: Warli figures are painted with a white rice-paste pigment.

stem: The Gond paintings are built up from patterns of __________.
solution: Gond paintings are built from intricate patterns of dots and dashes.

stem: Folk and tribal art forms have gained __________ in modern times, moving onto paper and canvas.
solution: These arts have gained wider popularity and commercial value, adapting to new media.

stem: The Madhubani painting styles include Kachni (line) and __________ (colour-filling).
solution: Madhubani styles include Kachni (line work) and Bharni (colour filling).

stem: Folk art traditions are usually passed down __________.
options: from generation to generation within families/communities
solution: Folk art traditions are passed down through families and communities across generations.

stem: The Jagannath cult of Puri is closely linked with the __________ painting tradition.
solution: Pattachitra painting is closely linked with the Jagannath cult of Puri.

stem: Folk and tribal art usually depicts __________.
options: nature, deities, daily life and community rituals
solution: Folk and tribal art depicts nature, deities, daily life and community rituals.

stem: The Warli tribe's paintings reflect their close relationship with __________.
solution: Warli paintings reflect the tribe's close relationship with nature.

stem: Pattachitra is painted on a specially prepared cloth called __________.
solution: Pattachitra is painted on a patta — cloth treated with a chalk-and-gum coating.

stem: The revival and marketing of folk arts today helps to __________.
solution: Reviving and marketing folk arts helps preserve traditions and support artisans.

stem: The subject of many Madhubani paintings includes __________.
options: gods, weddings and nature (fish, birds, trees)
solution: Madhubani paintings depict gods, weddings and nature motifs like fish, birds and trees.

stem: The tradition of painting scrolls that are used while singing or narrating a story is seen in __________.
solution: Phad, Pattachitra and Cheriyal scrolls are used with storytelling and song.

stem: Folk art forms are important because they represent the __________ of India.
solution: Folk art forms represent India's diverse living cultural heritage.

stem: Warli painting uses mainly __________ colours.
solution: Warli painting is mainly white figures on an earthy brown/red background.

stem: Which of the following is a tribal art form?
solution: Gond painting is a tribal art form; the others are courtly/colonial schools.

stem: Kalamkari literally means '__________ work'.
solution: Kalamkari means 'pen work', referring to the pen used to draw with natural dyes.

stem: The natural black dye in Kalamkari is often made using __________.
solution: Kalamkari's black is traditionally made from a fermented jaggery-and-iron solution.

stem: The living art traditions show that Indian art is not only in __________ but also among the people.
solution: Living traditions show Indian art thrives among the people, not only in museums and palaces.

stem: Madhubani painting received recognition and reached a wider audience when it moved from walls to __________.
solution: Madhubani gained wider recognition when it moved from walls to paper and cloth.

stem: Folk and tribal art are usually created for __________ rather than for sale originally.
solution: Folk and tribal art was originally created for ritual, festival and decoration.

stem: The scroll paintings of Bengal narrating stories are called __________.
solution: Bengal's storytelling scrolls are the Patua (Bengal Pattachitra) scrolls.

stem: The variety of India's living art traditions reflects its __________.
solution: The variety of living traditions reflects India's cultural and regional diversity.

stem: The importance of preserving living art traditions lies in maintaining __________.
solution: Preserving these traditions maintains cultural continuity and supports artisans.

stem: The living art traditions demonstrate the __________ nature of Indian art.
solution: Living traditions demonstrate the continuous and evolving nature of Indian art.

stem: Which art form is famous for depicting Lord Jagannath?
solution: Pattachitra of Odisha is famous for depicting Lord Jagannath.
